# Swath — Performance

_Measured, not asserted: every number was produced by a named `just` recipe at a stated commit
and is diffable against a committed artifact under `docs/perf/`; where a historic claim did not
reproduce, the honest number is here instead._

## 1. Method, before numbers

**One recipe per instrument** — what CI runs is what produced the tables here. **Committed
artifacts are the ground truth** — a PR that changes a number changes an artifact, so the diff
*is* the claim review. **Enforcement over aspiration** — the harness that measures the headline
asserts it under a budget on every commit; the other baselines are regression evidence.

## 2. Environment (full disclosure)

One developer laptop: Apple M2 Max (12 cores, 32 GB), macOS 26.5.2 arm64; rustc 1.97.1
(criterion on the `bench` profile; e2e/load hit the release binary in a linux/arm64 container);
oha 1.15.0 (pinned) plus a unique-URL Python driver for the cold burst. Serve dataset: the
committed HLS fixtures (~1.4 MB, real swath-edge nodata); referencer dataset: the pinned
VNP09GA conformance granule (8.2 MB HDF-EOS5, 1,551 chunk refs — ADR 0008). Not controlled:
thermals, background load, page cache — "cold" means "first run in the recipe invocation". A
laptop, not a lab.

## 3. Instruments: which recipe, which artifact

The stamp table above maps each instrument to its recipe and artifact; methodology lives with
each instrument — `crates/swath-e2e` (§4), the criterion benches (§5),
`tests/load/load.{sh,py}` (§6), the `perf-referencer` recipe (§7),
`tests/load/temporal.{sh,py}` (§8).

## 4. Ingest-to-pixel (the headline)

The north-star metric (REQUIREMENTS §3), measured end to end through the real stack by the
harness that pdiff-verifies the tile's pixels against goldens.

<!-- table:i2p (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| metric | measured | enforced budget |
|---|---:|---:|
| ingest_to_pixel_ms | 646 ms | 10000 ms |
<!-- /table:i2p -->

**Enforcement.** `just e2e` asserts `ingest_to_pixel_ms` under the 10,000 ms budget on every
commit — deliberately ~20× above measured values, catching structural regressions rather than
runner noise; tightening it is a deliberate act.

Single-request latency is visible in the load table (cold live renders: p50 <!-- number:cold-p50-approx -->~660 ms<!-- /number:cold-p50-approx --> for z15 tiles; hot cache hits: p50 <!-- number:hot-p50-approx -->~23 ms<!-- /number:hot-p50-approx --> at c=32 — §6).

## 6. Concurrency and the async-vs-blocking boundary

`just load` is the concurrency measurement the e2e never takes (ARCHITECTURE §16.7):

<!-- table:load (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| scenario | requests | errors | rps | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | max ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| healthz — idle baseline | 84450 | 0 | 16883.2 | 0.23 | 0.3 | 0.36 | 3.84 |
| (a) hot-cache tile storm | 26306 | 0 | 1313.7 | 23.33 | 34.91 | 41.79 | 72.57 |
| (b) cold live-render burst | 128 | 0 | 11.5 | 660.61 | 1140.7 | 1221.21 | 1231.08 |
| (c) mixed tile storm | 813 | 0 | 20.1 | 852.82 | 1983.87 | 2051.72 | 2096.35 |
| (c) healthz UNDER WARPS | 190707 | 0 | 9533.8 | 0.39 | 0.64 | 0.97 | 30.35 |

SSE `/traces` under the mixed storm: survived the 45s window: **yes** (828 trace events received).
<!-- /table:load -->

The §16.7 evidence is the last two rows: under c=16 clients hammering the heaviest live warps,
`/healthz` p99 stays sub-millisecond and the SSE subscription survives — render work is not
starving the async control plane.

## 7. Referencer: the historic "40×" and "14 ms" claims, re-run

**Provenance.** Prototype 0001 (immutable) measured generation on the VNP09GA granule:
*"referencer-rs 29 ms cold / 14 ms warm; virtualizarr sidecar 876 ms cold / ~556–574 ms warm …
Rust ≤ sidecar by ~40× warm"* — the Rust generator timed **in-process**, the sidecar **as a
subprocess**. `just perf-referencer` re-measures both the same way — full-process wall clock,
release profile, same granule — which is *less* flattering to Rust:

<!-- table:referencer (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| generator | command | cold | warm (median) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| referencer-rs | `target/release/swath ingest reference <path-to>/VNP09GA.A2012019.h33v12.002.2023122182434.h5 --output target/referencer/perf-rs.vmanifest.json` | 456.2 ms | 13.8 ms |
| virtualizarr-sidecar | `python/.venv/bin/swath-referencer <path-to>/VNP09GA.A2012019.h33v12.002.2023122182434.h5` | 13278.0 ms | 545.6 ms |

Warm-generation ratio (sidecar / Rust): **~39.5x** in Rust's favor (10 runs; full-process wall clock; run 1 = cold, warm = median of the rest).
<!-- /table:referencer -->

**Verdicts** (all 10 raw samples in the artifact):

- **"14 ms warm" — reproduces.** Warm median <!-- number:ref-warm-ms -->13.8 ms<!-- /number:ref-warm-ms --> for the production release binary,
  full-process.
- **"~40× warm" — reproduces.** Sidecar warm median <!-- number:ref-sidecar-warm-ms -->545.6 ms<!-- /number:ref-sidecar-warm-ms --> / Rust <!-- number:ref-warm-ms -->13.8 ms<!-- /number:ref-warm-ms --> = **<!-- number:ref-ratio -->39.5×<!-- /number:ref-ratio -->**, squarely
  in line with the prototype's ~40×.
- **The cold numbers are NOT comparable and we don't headline them** — both are
  first-invocation-after-build effects; steady-state (warm) is the figure we claim.

Both generators emit byte-range-equivalent manifests — the gated conformance test
(`just test-referencer`) — so the comparison is between implementations producing
verified-identical output.

**Honest accounting.** Production runs the generator per granule as a process, so
per-invocation is the honest unit — but stated plainly, this is an architecture result (no
interpreter, no warm-up, a 4.5 MB binary vs a ~273 MB venv), not a claim that Rust scans HDF5
chunk indexes <!-- number:ref-ratio-approx -->~40×<!-- /number:ref-ratio-approx --> faster than h5py once Python is already warm.

## 8. Temporal frame-serving and overview-backed tiles

The M7 measurement (`just load-temporal`): the time slider's serving path (ADR 0015, #223) and
the materialized overview path (#183/#218), on the §2 stack plus the six-date Park Fire series
dropped mid-run. The report *fails* unless every request's recorded decision mix is exactly
what each scenario is defined by.

**(d) Animation frames** — every interior z14 tile of the fire footprint, `datetime=` for each
of the six dates in order: cold (every dated frame a live render) p50
<!-- number:frame-cold-p50-approx -->~350 ms<!-- /number:frame-cold-p50-approx --> per tile; the
same loop again is all granule-scoped cache hits at p50
<!-- number:frame-hot-p50-approx -->~8 ms<!-- /number:frame-hot-p50-approx --> — the temporal
cache identity (granule id, not datetime string) makes a replayed animation cheap.

**(e) The overview ladder** — one tile per zoom rung, tile cache cleared per request, so each
rung measures its *render* path: z12 plans full-resolution live (p50
<!-- number:ov-live-p50-approx -->~260 ms<!-- /number:ov-live-p50-approx -->); pre-materialize,
z10 serves the embedded ×2 overview; after `swath materialize`
(<!-- number:materialize-ms -->578 ms<!-- /number:materialize-ms --> for every layer of both
datasets, mid-scenario) the same z10 tile plans the materialized ×4 level at p50
<!-- number:ov-pyramid-p50-approx -->~130 ms<!-- /number:ov-pyramid-p50-approx -->. Each rung's
overview *level* is pinned from the SSE trace envelopes.

<!-- table:temporal (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| scenario | requests | errors | rps | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | max ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (d) frame loop, cold (all Live) | 54 | 0 | 14.6 | 345.99 | 606.77 | 619.69 | 619.69 |
| (d) frame loop, hot (all cache hits) | 54 | 0 | 150.7 | 7.91 | 270.43 | 271.12 | 271.12 |
| (e) z12 — Live (full resolution) | 24 | 0 | 3.7 | 259.24 | 269.31 | 288.11 | 288.11 |
| (e) z10 pre-materialize (embedded ov. ×2) | 24 | 0 | 4.0 | 230.59 | 257.88 | 290.6 | 290.6 |
| (e) z11 post-materialize (pyramid ov. ×2) | 24 | 0 | 3.7 | 246.59 | 296.56 | 317.68 | 317.68 |
| (e) z10 post-materialize (pyramid ov. ×4) | 24 | 0 | 6.6 | 134.75 | 146.19 | 162.52 | 162.52 |

Frame decisions (`x-swath-trace`): cold {"live": 54}, hot {"cache_hit": 54}. Overview-rung decisions (SSE envelopes, level included): live_z12 {"live": 24}; embedded_z10 {"overview:2": 24}; pyramid_z11 {"overview:2": 24}; pyramid_z10 {"overview:4": 24}.
<!-- /table:temporal -->

A dated frame pays the ordinary live price on first touch and the cache-hit price on replay;
the ×4 level reads a quarter the pixels of the ×2 fallback.

## 9. `run_udf`: user code in the live tile path

Sandboxed WASM UDFs run inline on the render lane (ADR 0018), so the ADR 0012 async-vs-blocking
posture is what they must not break. The stage benches (§5) add `eval_udf_ndvi` — the reference
`examples/udf/ndvi` module through the wasmtime executor, asserted bit-identical to the
`eval_ndvi_rdylgn` band-math row beside it — and `udf_instantiate_warm`, the pooled-`Store`
cost the tile path pays per call. `just load-udf` then publishes two `run_udf` services and
storms them under the §6 (c)-style mixed load with concurrent `/healthz` + SSE `/traces` probes:

<!-- table:udf-load (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| scenario | requests | errors | rps | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | max ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (u) UDF mixed storm (Live NDVI + cache, buster on) | 4147 | 0 | 102.4 | 5.45 | 1230.98 | 1357.67 | 1453.55 |
| (u) healthz UNDER the UDF storm | 188264 | 0 | 9411.9 | 0.39 | 0.66 | 0.96 | 30.13 |
| (f) fuel-bomb storm — every tile refused | 637 | 637 | 15.7 | 886.7 | 1340.67 | 1370.81 | 1410.99 |
| (f) healthz UNDER the fuel-bomb refusals | 190614 | 0 | 9529.5 | 0.39 | 0.63 | 0.92 | 20.7 |

ADR 0012 signals — UDF storm: `/healthz` p99 0.96 ms (trigger 50.0 ms), SSE survived (4162 events), tripped: **no**. Fuel bomb (refused, zero collateral): `/healthz` p99 0.92 ms, SSE survived (0 events); tile 500 RFC 7807 fuel, preview 400 `ProcessGraphComplexity`; tripped: **no**.
<!-- /table:udf-load -->

**The UDF storm.** The reference NDVI module, hammered with the cache cleared every 250 ms (the
§6 (c) buster) so the render lane keeps re-rendering *through* the module — every probe's Live
sample charges the same deterministic `udf_fuel_used`, interleaved with the cache hits the
buster races. Under that load `/healthz` p99 holds at
<!-- number:udf-storm-healthz-p99 -->0.96 ms<!-- /number:udf-storm-healthz-p99 --> against the 50 ms
ADR 0012 reopen trigger and the SSE subscription survives: user code on the render lane does not
starve the control plane.

**The fuel bomb, refused with zero collateral.** A runaway-loop module publishes just as cleanly
(its registration probes are constant-time) and is refused only where it runs — the tile path
answers a 500 RFC 7807 problem naming the exhausted fuel budget, `POST /result` answers
`400 ProcessGraphComplexity` (refusal over degradation, ADR 0014) — while `/healthz` p99 is
<!-- number:udf-fuelbomb-healthz-p99 -->0.92 ms<!-- /number:udf-fuelbomb-healthz-p99 --> and the
SSE stream stays up: refusing user code costs the control plane nothing.

Scenario-integrity violations (a storm that never runs the module, a bomb that is not refused)
*fail* the report; the ADR 0012 signals are recorded and verdicted, never a build break — a trip
is a maintainer lane-decision on committed evidence (the pooled-lane executor behind the
`UdfExecutor` choke point is the designed mitigation, ADR 0018's rollback seam).

## 10. What we don't claim

Bounded honesty: **fixture scale** (~1.4 MB of fixtures, one 8 MB granule — nothing about
multi-terabyte catalogs or granules that dwarf RAM); **single node, loopback** (no
TLS/CDN/scaling claims — the read-only recipe in `deploy/README.md` is exercised, not
measured); **local storage**; **tested concurrency only** (up to c=32,
seconds-to-minutes windows); **microbenches are isolated stages** (§6 samples interference);
**one machine, uncontrolled** (diff same-machine baselines only); **the
<!-- number:ref-ratio-approx -->~40×<!-- /number:ref-ratio-approx --> ratio is per-invocation,
one granule, one format** (§7); **CI runners are slower and noisier** (the 10 s budget is sized
for that).

Several of these gaps are intended future work, not permanent posture — real-ingress behavior,
multi-node scale, and larger-than-fixture datasets are on the candidate list in
[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md).

## 11. Regenerating this document

```bash
just bench-baseline    # criterion benches -> bench-baseline.json
just load              # load scenarios -> load-baseline.{json,md}
just load-temporal     # frame loop + overview ladder -> temporal-baseline.{json,md}
just load-udf          # run_udf storm + fuel bomb -> load-udf-baseline.{json,md}
just perf-i2p          # typed e2e -> i2p-baseline.json
just perf-referencer   # referencer bake-off -> referencer-baseline.json
just perf-doc          # regenerate every table AND every inline number marker
```

Commit the artifact diffs alongside the regenerated tables; the PR should say why numbers
moved. Headline figures quoted in prose live inside inline `number:<key>` HTML-comment marker
pairs that `just perf-doc` fills (idempotent) and the docs-check gate verifies
(`crates/swath-cli/src/docs_check/numbers.rs`). To quote a headline number, add a marker with an
existing key and run `just perf-doc`; never type the number by hand.
